title: Verlet Physics 3D — Mass-Spring Cloth
author: Karsten Schmidt (toxiclibs.physics, 2008) / Thomas Jakobsen (Verlet integration, 2001)
description: A 3D mass-spring system integrated with Verlet position-based dynamics and Jakobsen-style constraint relaxation. Particles carry position, previous position, mass, and a 'locked' flag. Springs are length-preserving (distance) constraints between pairs of particles; bending constraints span three-particle chains; spherical and box constraints keep particles inside (or outside) a region. Each step: integrate (x' = x + (x - x_prev) * damping + a * dt²), then relax constraints 8-16 iterations. Karsten's toxiclibs implementation is the reference Java port of the algorithm and underpins the cloth simulations, soft-body demos, and 'wobbly jelly' toys used across the openFrameworks and Processing communities. The 3D version is the natural extension of the 2D version (toxi_openframeworks/ParticleSpring2D) and demonstrates how the same Verlet abstraction generalizes to spatial simulations.
math_essence: Verlet integration: x_new = 2·x - x_prev + a·dt². Damping: x_new = x + (1-d)·(x - x_prev) + a·dt². Constraint relaxation: for each spring with rest length L and stiffness k, move each end by ±(k/2)·(current_length - L)·normalized_direction. Bending constraints: a chain (a, b, c) gets rest_angle preservation via a perpendicular-offset projection. NaN/Infinity guard on every step. Floor plane: y >= 0 with reflection (v_new = -v_old * restitution).

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Cloth side length in world units.

parameters.name: stiffness
parameters.description: Spring stiffness (clamped 0..1 in the Jakobsen style).

source_provenance: toxiclibs.physics.VerletPhysics3D (Karsten Schmidt, c. 2008) — see https://github.com/postspectacular/toxiclibs. Algorithm: Jakobsen 2001 'Hitman' GDC paper on position-based dynamics. Pure numpy implementation here (no Java dependency).
